title: Samsung Galaxy Fit pulse record supporting referral and ablation for Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
summary: A Samsung Galaxy Fit band recorded a pulse of 188 beats per minute in a woman in South Korea, and with a routine electrocardiogram the record supported her referral for a successful ablation in 2020.
account: A 26-year-old woman worked 12-hour days in a multinational company's quality control department in South Korea. Before she bought a Samsung Galaxy Fit (SM-R370) band, she had had palpitations for four years, and an emergency visit on 9 June 2020 ended with symptomatic treatment only. The band measures pulse by photoplethysmography. On 18 June 2020 she experienced severe palpitations for hours, and her band recorded a peak resting pulse rate of 188 beats per minute. The next day, 19 June 2020, a routine health-examination 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) was taken while she was asymptomatic. It showed a shortened PR interval and delta waves, establishing Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome. The authors of the case report are from the Department of Occupational and Environmental Medicine at Kangbuk Samsung Hospital. They recommended an electrophysiology study based on the ECG, her symptoms and the pulse records from the band. Electrophysiology study and radiofrequency catheter ablation of the bypass tract followed on 29 June 2020 at the authors' hospital. After discharge she monitored for recurrence with a smartwatch. The case was reported in Annals of Occupational and Environmental Medicine on 24 March 2021. A 2024 report describes a Galaxy Watch 4 ECG capturing polymorphic ventricular tachycardia that led to a diagnosis of vasospastic angina in another patient. In a prospective study published on 19 April 2026, Italian cardiologists found that 30 of 59 patients with palpitations recorded an arrhythmia on a smartwatch ECG within three months. Of the 59 patients, 15 used Samsung watches, and the authors do not report results by brand.
purpose: The Galaxy Fit's optical sensor is built to track heart rate, and the Galaxy Watch ECG app to record single-lead ECGs for rhythm assessment. The benefit came from those functions.
system: Samsung Galaxy Fit heart-rate monitor and Galaxy Watch ECG app
model_version: Galaxy Fit SM-R370 (event); Galaxy Watch Series 4 in echo

ratings.reason: A young worker's band documented a tachycardia of 188 beats per minute. With her symptoms and a routine electrocardiogram showing Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome the next day, the band's record supported her referral for an electrophysiology study. Successful radiofrequency catheter ablation came 11 days after the recorded episode. The benefit to her was material, although the diagnosis itself came from the routine electrocardiogram.

display.answer: The case is known only from the case report by clinicians at Kangbuk Samsung Hospital. The 2024 systematic review reports one patient who used a Samsung Galaxy Fit. The 2024 case report from Haifa and the 2026 Italian study concern other patients, and Samsung wrote the clearance summary for its ECG app.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: A Samsung Galaxy Fit band recorded a pulse of 188 beats per minute in a woman in South Korea, and with a routine electrocardiogram the record supported her referral for a successful ablation in 2020.
fields.account: A 26-year-old woman worked 12-hour days in a multinational company's quality control department in South Korea. Before she bought a Samsung Galaxy Fit (SM-R370) band, she had had palpitations for four years, and an emergency visit on 9 June 2020 ended with symptomatic treatment only. The band measures pulse by photoplethysmography. On 18 June 2020 she experienced severe palpitations for hours, and her band recorded a peak resting pulse rate of 188 beats per minute. The next day, 19 June 2020, a routine health-examination 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) was taken while she was asymptomatic. It showed a shortened PR interval and delta waves, establishing Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome. The authors of the case report are from the Department of Occupational and Environmental Medicine at Kangbuk Samsung Hospital. They recommended an electrophysiology study based on the ECG, her symptoms and the pulse records from the band. Electrophysiology study and radiofrequency catheter ablation of the bypass tract followed on 29 June 2020 at the authors' hospital. After discharge she monitored for recurrence with a smartwatch. The case was reported in Annals of Occupational and Environmental Medicine on 24 March 2021. A 2024 report describes a Galaxy Watch 4 ECG capturing polymorphic ventricular tachycardia that led to a diagnosis of vasospastic angina in another patient. In a prospective study published on 19 April 2026, Italian cardiologists found that 30 of 59 patients with palpitations recorded an arrhythmia on a smartwatch ECG within three months. Of the 59 patients, 15 used Samsung watches, and the authors do not report results by brand.

value.text: The wearable recorded the rapid heart-rate episode for later clinical assessment.
The initial event involved a Galaxy Fit SM-R370. A later report involved a Galaxy Watch Series 4.
The Galaxy Fit recorded pulse optically, including a peak resting rate of 188 beats per minute during the woman's symptoms.

produced_by: The wearer uses a Samsung Galaxy band or watch with heart-rate tracking or the ECG app
A symptomatic arrhythmia occurs while the device is worn and the reading or trace is shown to a clinician
A clinician confirms the rhythm and treats it
must_hold: The device recording is reviewed promptly
A 12-lead ECG or inpatient monitoring is available for confirmation
Definitive therapy (ablation, drugs, device) is accessible

echoes.setting: 54-year-old male recreational athlete, Haifa, Israel (authors' institution); Galaxy Watch 4 single-lead ECG during syncope showed polymorphic VT; vasospastic angina with coronary disease, verapamil and wearable defibrillator, no events at one year (publication date)
